A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CachePrune. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on SQuAD, HotpotQA and WildChat, alongside pruning ablations, neuron analyses and code/text attack transfer results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original model evaluations, ablations, cross-attack transfer tests, adaptive attacks and additional quality metrics.

M1.justification: The probability-difference loss, activation-times-gradient attribution, maximum aggregation, normalized Φ restriction and context-cache masking are retained. The newly named attribution and intervention stages elaborate existing components. The threshold formula revision does not establish a change to the described top-fraction pruning procedure.

E1.justification: SQuAD, HotpotQA and WildChat remain the datasets. v2 substantially expands adversarial test scenarios through controlled transfer across attack-instruction families and defense-adaptive GCG attacks, including transferred attack sequences (Figure 5 and Appendices F–G).

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Sandwich as an evaluated defense alongside the retained Vanilla, Delimiting, Datamarking and Encode_Base64 comparators. Newly discussed detection and attribution methods are cited rather than evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds Phi-3.5-mini-instruct (3.8B), attribution sample-size sweeps of 4/8/12, and ROUGE-1/2/L and BERTScore evaluation. Its new adaptive protocol optimizes attack tokens over 24 examples, normally using 10 tokens and 20 epochs, with 30-token and 100-epoch variants. Original default benchmark settings remain.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether restricting pruning to Φ preserves quality, sensitivity to attribution sample count, transfer across attack instructions, and robustness to adaptive attacks and their optimization budgets (Tables 5–12; Figures 5 and 9). The original token-count, masking-strength, pruning-ratio, layer-distribution and code/text transfer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over three trials and use ± entries. v2 does not establish additional repetitions, seed disclosure or a new uncertainty-estimation practice. Added result rows and changed uncertainty values are changes to results.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial model, baseline, ablation, transfer, adaptive-attack and metric results. Table 7 reports adaptive-attack ASR of 7.71±0.63 for CachePrune versus 97.89 for Vanilla. Original benchmark means are retained, while Table 1's Llama3/SQuAD attack-F1 changes from 22.84±0.18 to 22.84±0.49. Some new deltas are inconsistent: Delimiting ASR rising from 23.60 to 100 implies +76.40, whereas Table 7 prints +72.14.

T1.justification: Equation 5 revises the pruning-threshold formula from a supremum expression to an infimum expression using an indicator expectation. The DPO bound, entropy decomposition, Lemma 1 and their proofs are otherwise retained and relocated to Appendices B–D. The newly stated standard F1 formulas add explanation.

C1.justification: The central defense, efficiency and response-quality claims remain. v2 softens the loss's theoretical framing from being induced from a DPO upper bound to sharing its insights, and its discussion explicitly adds robustness and generalizability across attack types.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations concerning known context boundaries, trigger tokens as implicit planning, free-form QA metrics, and adaptive-attack optimization limitations. It also introduces an erroneous interpretation: Section 4.2 says increasing α raises ASR, reversing v1's explanation despite the retained table showing ASR falling from 13.50 to 6.40 as α increases from 0.3 to 1.5.

D1.justification: v2 supplies evaluation code snippets for F1, ROUGE and BERTScore, identifies gpt-4-1106-preview as the judge, and includes complete judging prompts. It also documents attack construction, initialization and optimization settings. Details about the retained free-form QA evaluation and sampling procedure are expanded without establishing changes to those original procedures.

R1.justification: Section 3 substantially expands positioning relative to detection/filtering defenses and attribution/activation patching. It explicitly locates the contribution in using attribution to understand data versus instructions rather than introducing an entirely new intervention technique, and discusses shared context-boundary assumptions. Additional references support the new attacks, model and metrics.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Section 2 gains separate attribution and intervention subsections, while DPO motivation moves into Appendix B and baseline/metric descriptions move into Appendix A. Expanded appendices reorganize sampling explanations, evaluation details and analyses.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn, and v2 adds transfer heatmaps and adaptive-training plots. Table 1 gains model and baseline rows plus metric-direction indicators. Original ablation tables and layer histograms move into the appendices, alongside substantial new ablation, adaptive-attack and metric tables.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central robustness and quality-preservation claims through adaptive attacks, cross-attack transfer, the Φ ablation and additional quality metrics. Evaluation code and judging prompts address important reproducibility gaps in v1. These gains outweigh localized reporting errors, including the reversed α interpretation and incorrect Table 7 baseline deltas, although those errors weaken confidence in some explanations.
